environment: word-finally, except in very careful speech
notes: 'pw is made without the lip rounding that occurs when pw is at the beginning or in the middle of words. The raising of the back of the tongue, however, still takes place' (p. 27).
'Like pw, mw has an unrounded velarized allophone at the end of words' (p. 31).
'At the end of words, in careful speech, all stops in Ponapean are released ... Except at the end of words in careful speech, stops are otherwise non-released' (p. 29).

s 'undergoes varying degrees of palatalization ... s usually sounds as if it were somewhere between English s (as in sip) and sh (as in ship)' (p. 30).
'For some speakers, the fricative part of the pronunciation of t is very slight, so that t sounds more like a stop' (p. 30).
'When n precedes t [the retroflex affricate] ... it too is pronounced in this retroflexed position' (p. 33).
l 'is voiced and is also slightly palatalized' (p. 33).
